headline: Elon Musk Has a Tesla Problem He Can’t Seem to Fix
summary: Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) has been one of the most remarkable wealth creators in stock market history. But with Tesla shares falling roughly 20% this year, investors are beginning to ask a difficult question: Has Wall Street finally lost patience with Elon Musk? In this episode, 24/7 Wall St. co-founder Doug McIntyre joins senior writer and editor Lee Jackson to discuss why Tesla is dramatically underperforming many of its Magnificent Seven peers, and whether the company's biggest problem is Elon Musk himself. For years, Musk has argued that Tesla is much more than an electric vehicle manufacturer. He has promised revolutionary advances in artificial intelligence, humanoid robotics, autonomous driving, and robotaxis. Yet many of those promises have taken far longer to materialize than investors expected. Doug explains why Tesla's extraordinary valuation may be increasingly difficult to justify if investors begin treating it primarily as an automotive company rather than an emerging AI powerhouse. The discussion also explores Tesla's electric vehicle sales, its popularity in California, the impact of gasoline prices, growing skepticism surrounding Musk's ambitious timelines, and what upcoming third-quarter earnings could mean for TSLA shareholders. Is Tesla still one of the market's greatest growth stories, or has the Elon Musk premium finally started to disappear?
